reviewer: Claude Code (AI assistant). Not an independent human review.
method: Round three of 1793, under the rule 'every story alike' (11 November 2026): the items that rounds one and two held back for framing, counted item by item at the year's rule of 6 newspapers with phrase searches on all 1,751 pages in both transcriptions, reading of every hit, loose keyword searches of the papers in print without a hit, and scan checks of each admitted passage
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

new_groups.label: News from Cap Français, June 1793
new_groups.definition: Two accounts of events at Cap Français, in the French colony of Saint-Domingue, from 18 to 23 June 1793, as American papers printed them in July and August from arrivals at New York: Captain Fanning's account, and the report of the passengers of the brig Mary, who put the dead at six to nine hundred, 'instead of 10 thousand as we heard', as most papers print it. Contains those two groups; the wider coverage is not included. Each is an account at second hand.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: Captain Fanning's account of Cap Français
new_groups.definition: Printings of the account given at New York by Captain John Fanning of the brig Union, 14 days from Cap Français (New York, 9 July 1793): on 18 June the civil commissioners Sonthonax and Polverel arrived at the Cape and suspended the governor, Galbaud; by his account they then encouraged 'a number of mulattoes' to come into town, who armed the enslaved people of the town 'to assist in destroying all the whites'; between 8 and 10 thousand people were killed from 20 June; and the town was plundered and burnt, with not more than 50 houses standing when he sailed on the 23rd with a fleet of 250 sail. One ship captain's account. Three papers print it under the heading 'HORRID NEWS!'.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: The brig Mary's passengers on Cap Français
new_groups.definition: Printings of a New York report of late July 1793 on the brig Mary, Captain Langdon, from Cap Français, which she left on 9 July: her forty passengers said that from six to nine hundred people lost their lives 'in the affair of the 20th' (most papers add 'instead of 10 thousand as we heard'; the Patowmac Guardian prints 'two thousand'), that not more than two thirds of the town was burnt, that 'upwards of 20,000 mulattoes and blacks are now under arms there', that 'the negroes never came in from the country on the late occasion', and that the Spaniards had taken a town and were on the march. The passengers' account, at second hand.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: The War Office on the treaty commissioners, September 1793
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Philadelphia paragraph of early September 1793: by an express to the War Office from the commissioners for treating with the Indian nations north of the Ohio, they 'were not able even to effect a meeting' with the nations assembled at the rapids of the Miami river; the nations' deputation 'insisted upon the Ohio as the boundary between them and the United States', and, 'as so extensive a concession was inadmissible', the commissioners left on 17 August. It names the Wyandots, Delawares, Shawanese and Miamis as 'determined for war', says that a considerable part of them were for peace, and that the Six Nations, with Captain Brandt (Brant) and his Mohawks, urged peace. The United States government's account, as the papers printed it.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: A letter from German Creek, 16 August 1793: an expedition across the Tennessee
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter dated German Creek, Territory South of the Ohio, 16 August 1793, written to the editor of a Winchester paper (2 September) and printed from it: the writer reports that on 4 August Colonel Daugherty of Jefferson county crossed the Tennessee with 180 men to 'the valley Indian towns', where by his account they killed nine men and two women, took seven prisoners, burnt twenty towns and villages and destroyed crops, with five of their own men wounded. He adds that the frontier inhabitants are 'in close forts', and argues for a large company raised 'under the sanction of government' to give the towns, in his words, 'a severe flogging, in order to bring them to a sense of their duty, and teach them to pay some respect to treaties'. One writer's account.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the 6-paper threshold for 1793).

dispositions_summary.method: Round three of 1793. On 11 November 2026 the owner set the rule 'every story alike': a reviewed story is described by what kind of text it is and whose account, in the papers' own words, never as what happened; sensitive subjects get no special treatment. Items that earlier rounds held back for framing are therefore counted by the year's own rule, exactly like any other item: what reaches it is admitted, what does not stays out. As before, an excerpt ends before the names of private people where it can, and stories that turn on private people stay out. The items rounds one and two left out for framing were read again with phrase searches over all 1,751 pages of 1793 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round3.json, phrase_hits_round3.json), every hit was read, the papers in print without a hit were searched with loose keywords (no missed printing), and every admitted printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/batch_09.json and batch_10.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round3.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: For 1793 a story needs one printed item found in 6 or more newspapers, counted item by item, the two titles of a renamed paper once (the owner's decision of 10 November 2026). Where several items belong to one affair, each is its own group under a parent story; a sub-story may have fewer papers than the threshold when its parent reaches it. As for the 4-paper documents of Dumouriez's defection in round one, items in 4 papers are not admitted as sub-stories.

counted_item_by_item.The War Office paragraph: 6 papers (NGz 4 September, GUS 7 September, PG 16 September, NHG and AHL 17 September, CI 25 September). Two other items on the commissioners are in 3 papers each and not part of the group: their letter from the mouth of Detroit river (GUS, PG, AHL twice) and a paragraph on the nations' answer of 2 August (NGz, PG, CI).
counted_item_by_item.The German Creek letter: 6 papers (NGz and GUS 11 September, PG 16 September, NHG and AHL 24 September, CI 2 October); PG prints it from a Georgetown paper of 7 September.
counted_item_by_item.Cap Français: Captain Fanning's account (New York, 9 July; NGz 10 July, NHG and AHL 16 July, MIR and PG 22 July, GUS on the issue filed under 23 July, which is of 13 July: 6 papers) and the brig Mary's passengers' report (GUS 27 July, NGz 31 July, PG 5 August, NHG and AHL 6 August, CI 14 August: 6 papers) are two items about the same days; each reaches the threshold and each is its own group under the parent 'News from Cap Français, June 1793'.

not_admitted.The civil commissioners' proclamation of: 4 papers (NGz and GUS 27 July, NHG and AHL 13 August; NGz quotes it again in a commentary of 21 August): below the threshold, and not a sub-story, as for the 4-paper documents of Dumouriez's defection.
not_admitted.The letter of Polverel and Sonthonax to: 4 papers (GUS 29 May, NGz 1 June, AHL 18 June, MIR 24 June): below the threshold.
not_admitted.The Fugitive Slave Act: 'An act respecting fugitives from justice, and persons escaping from the service of their masters': its text is in 2 papers (MIR 11 March, GUS 17 April); its title is also in the lists of the session's acts (NGz 6 March, GUS 9 March, KG 13 April), which are a different item. Below the threshold.
not_admitted.Private people (5 papers each): The prosecutions of the seamen Singleterry and Henfield, and a killing near Middletown, New Jersey: below the threshold, and stories that turn on private people stay out.
